agent_priors_used: Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): when a research portfolio converts fewer than one in twenty experiments into a validated capability, the marginal return on new hypotheses is usually lower than the marginal return on removing the instrument-level defects that make hypotheses unidentifiable. SPIDER's 0-of-395 promotion record and 65% recent MEASUREMENT_INVALID rate are SPIDER evidence; the inference that instrument repair now dominates hypothesis generation is my judgment from that evidence plus this prior.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): inherited or cached context in long-horizon agents is a known failure amplifier through staleness, path dependence and context salience, so an inheritance layer without a measured false-accept bound is a net risk rather than a neutral bet. This prior is why I rank C-FRESHNESS above another representation-learning thread for Graph; SPIDER's own evidence is only that C-FRESHNESS is HYPOTHESIS after 55 experiments, not that staleness has been observed to cause failures.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): benchmark success checks that are programmatically gameable make downstream cost and accuracy economics unfalsifiable, and reward hacking of agent benchmarks is a known failure pattern. This prior motivates assigning Intel a testbed-admissibility audit; SPIDER evidence supports only that Scout reported the claim about eight benchmarks, which is unverified external context, not a Codex result.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): in software engineering, the economics of incremental recompilation under partial change are governed by an environment property, change locality, that is usually treated as given and is almost never measured. Generalizing this to agent memory, the true edit-locality of a Web resource is the hidden variable that decides whether delta repair and freshness guards are worth anything. This prior motivates the Frontier mandate and is explicitly not a SPIDER observation; no SPIDER experiment has manipulated edit locality as a designed variable.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): a compilation-plus-invalidation algebra is a different level of description from a mechanism registry, and the two imply different internal architectures. SPIDER's Research 2.0 charter explicitly authorizes replacing internals when evidence warrants it, which is why I ask Frontier to attack the representation question rather than continue mining novelty-rate parameters.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): strong nulls require that the test be able to fail, and a null calibrated on a synthetic facade whose ground truth is known by construction is the cheapest possible demonstration that an apparatus is not merely returning a constant. This is the standard identifiability discipline and it is why the Physics mandate is validity-first rather than effect-first.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): a well-run external baseline that is executable locally is worth more to a research program than a precise summary of what that baseline claims, because it converts an unmeasurable comparison into a measurable one and it supplies a failure mode to differentiate against. This prior drives the Intel pivot.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: Versus the inherited third extraction round: I require all of the inherited design repairs, since they are excellent and they are exactly what the previous audit demanded, but they repair a question whose answer is established, and the lane is already in a 17-experiment C-CROSSSITE concentration, so continuing would be a textbook local attractor. Versus WebArena-Pro task-manifest analysis alone, which the Scout also proposes: useful for holdout design but not decision-changing, because it silently assumes the benchmark's success checks are trustworthy, which is precisely what component (a) tests. Versus HMT reproduction: genuinely valuable and a close structural analogue of SPIDER's Intent/Stage/Action hierarchy, but it competes with WebXSkill for one lane slot and WebXSkill is the closer analogue of SPIDER's actual mechanism, parameterized skills with URL-graph retrieval and executable deployment, so it is the higher-information single target; HMT remains a legitimate follow-on. Versus the reward-hacking audit alone: highest urgency but it delivers a constraint rather than a capability, and it leaves SPIDER with a validated measuring instrument and still no external system to be measured against. Versus a generic tooling or literature sweep: explicitly out of charter and out of scope for a Director cycle.

allocation.question: Is there a verified, site-identity-controlled, non-gameable external holdout together with a runnable external parameterized-mechanism baseline that SPIDER can actually be measured against, meaning concretely: (a) do the programmatic success checks of WebArena, WebChoreArena and WebArena-Pro admit automated reward-hacking to high apparent success, and if so which specific sub-checks remain trustworthy and which must be excluded; and (b) does WebXSkill (arXiv:2604.13318) run end-to-end on WebArena with its skill-extraction, URL-graph organization and grounded/guided deployment components individually present and independently verifiable, and what success delta does it produce under a harness that is simultaneously usable for SPIDER, with every artifact identity resolved and verified before any condition is scored, every reported number carrying its denominator and accounting convention, and a null control with real power against deliberate artifact-identity substitution?
allocation.rationale: Intel has run 71 experiments, 15 of the last 17 on C-CROSSSITE literature extraction, and the most recent packet's load-bearing finding was negative and now closes the question it set out to answer: no external source publishes a goal-to-artifact binding error rate, abstention rate or human-intervention rate in the four-part form, so C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE is unoccupied-AND-unmeasured rather than settled. Once the answer to a question is known, re-asking it with better hygiene has low marginal information, and the Scout's field report makes the alternative obvious: several external systems now implement SPIDER's architecture with runnable artifacts and published WebArena numbers, so the comparison SPIDER needs is against a running competitor rather than against prose. Intel's charter is precisely external competitors, datasets and baselines that change a live decision, and this changes two: it determines whether the cross-lane WebChoreArena and WebArena-Pro campaign that several lanes' candidate directions assume is admissible as measurement at all, and it hands Graph and Product a concrete external baseline for C-PARAM-INHERIT and C-LLM-INHERIT instead of the unmeasurable paper-claim bars that the last verdict had to correct. The Scout's report that major agent benchmarks including WebArena are reward-hackable to near-perfect scores is unverified external context, not SPIDER evidence, and I am treating it as a prior that is urgent enough to test and cheap enough to be worth a lane slot, because if it is true then every downstream cost and accuracy number SPIDER plans to produce is contaminated at the source. I am bundling the two components because (a) without it the campaign is inadmissible and (b) without (b) the campaign has no competitor to compare against.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: The dominant fact of the complete program map is that SPIDER has never converted accumulated work into a single validated product capability. Across 395 canonical experiments, codex/index.json records promote_to_product=true for ZERO packets; across 503 claim events, C-PRODUCT_CORE and SHIPPED never appear; the only two VALIDATED events in program history both belong to C-MEAS-VALID and are bounded 'plain HTTP localhost DISTRIBUTED' substrate results, not capabilities. Ten claims sit at HYPOTHESIS (7) or MEASUREMENT_INVALID (3), with C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY alone at EXPERIMENTAL. Decision distribution is 154 MEASUREMENT_INVALID, 59 FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING, 135 REVISE audits against 131 PASS, and in the last 84 experiments 55 (65%) ended MEASUREMENT_INVALID. The binding constraint is therefore no longer idea generation or claim design; it is instrument construction and identifiability. Reading the failure modes apart matters, because they have different owners. (a) Provisioning failure dominates Runtime: claim_streak 65, 15 of 15 recent experiments on C-MEAS-VALID, same_failure_count 3, last failure non-retryable, and the browser/writable branch is UNKNOWN because a Playwright private-helper gate failed before capture. (b) Identifiability failure dominates Product: EXP-PRODUCT-36272385776 was rejected as a non-identifying economic gate because B-COLD was priced by a fixed 3-request policy, and Frontier independently measured 0 of 1200 EXECUTABLE resolutions from the shipped kernel, so the inherited arm has no dynamic range anywhere in the program. (c) Design failure appears where a null lacked power against the failure that actually occurred, as in Intel's NC-FABRICATED-BINDING-CLAIMS. Second structural fact: exactly one instrument in this program is measurement-valid right now. C-MEAS-VALID retains an audited bounded DISTRIBUTED VALIDATED plain-HTTP ceiling (EXP-RUNTIME-36094450333, EXP-RUNTIME-36100549580), and both the Graph and Frontier handoffs independently converge on a verified-reachable stdlib multi-endpoint HTTP application. Every WebArena/BrowserGym/gpt-4o-mini path is a 106-experiment scar. Third and most important fact: SPIDER's central promise, that a later external agent pays only residual-novelty cost, has never been measured with an inherited-mechanism executor against a no-memory executor on the same tasks with honest end-to-end cost and an executable arm. The deopt ratchet showed episode-one compression versus cold but its inherited leg was NOT IDENTIFIED precisely because the kernel was non-executable; the economic gate was rejected for lack of dynamic range; and the LLM-inherit gate has never run to a valid verdict. C-LLM-INHERIT, C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY and C-PRODUCT-ECON are all currently non-identifying by construction, not by accident. The correct portfolio move is therefore not a new mechanism and not more infrastructure patience. It is to force executability, to force the freshness guard that makes reuse safe, to give the Physics apparatus a verdict on whether it can fail at all, to make the Runtime browser question terminal rather than open-ended, to convert Intel from prose extraction to a runnable competitor plus a testbed-admissibility audit, and to ask the one inherited-economics question nobody has asked, namely whether the second episode is as compressible as the first. This cycle is deliberately concentrated on making existing claims decidable rather than on adding claims.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The Scout brief changed three of my six decisions and sharpened a fourth. It changed Intel: I had provisionally continued the inherited third-round extraction with its (genuinely excellent) methodological repairs, but the Scout's report that WebXSkill, HMT, ColorBrowserAgent and cotomi Act are all running SPIDER's architecture with real WebArena numbers, combined with the last Intel verdict's own finding that no external source publishes a binding error rate in the four-part form, convinced me that a third extraction round has low marginal information while a runnable external competitor has high. The Scout's reward-hacking observation about WebArena success checks is the single most consequential item in the brief because the whole proposed cross-lane WebChoreArena/WebArena-Pro campaign, which several lanes' candidate directions assume, rests on those checks; I therefore made testbed admissibility an Intel deliverable that gates other lanes rather than a background concern. It changed Physics: I was prepared to PARK the lane outright on the strength of 80 experiments with no valid result, and the Scout's own framing of the failure (estimator validation on synthetic data is not the mission) sharpened my stopping rule into a single decisive validity experiment with a terminal consequence. It confirmed Runtime as CONTINUE rather than PIVOT, because the Scout's option (b), a stdlib-only substrate with seeded perturbations, is precisely what Graph and Frontier are already building on their own initiative, so Runtime abandoning browser capability would cost the program its only route to real-Web claims. It sharpened Frontier: the Scout's strongest candidate was the parent decomposition, and having the decomposition already frozen as EXP-FRONTIER-36272394045 made that a duplicate, which pushed me to the edit-locality question instead. Where I deliberately did not follow the Scout: I rejected its recommendation to PIVOT Product to the C-LLM-INHERIT gate and to PIVOT Physics to site-specific dynamical priors, for the same reason in both cases, namely that both depend on a real browser and an executable SPIDER arm, and SPIDER currently has neither. Ordering executability ahead of the viability test is the opposite of what the brief urged and I consider it the better reading of the Codex. I also did not treat the tunnel flags as quotas: Frontier, Physics, Runtime and Intel are all flagged, and I issue PIVOT to two of them but CONTINUE to the other two, because in each case the inherited direction survived the cognitive-reset test on its merits rather than by default.

inherited_next_question: Does a goal-to-artifact binding error rate exist in ANY external source - arXiv, official documentation, released artifacts, engineering write-ups or follow-up work, for any compiled or deterministic web executor including and beyond the five artifacts consulted here - reported as four separately measurable quantities (bind/compile success on a stated denominator, execution correctness conditional on binding, abstention-or-refusal rate, human-amendment-or-intervention rate), and specifically: does arXiv:2604.09718's MANDATORY per-blueprint human review gate (Section 3.3) have any published amendment rate anywhere, given that the paper publishes none and its only supporting table is an internal micro-benchmark on proprietary enterprise DOMs that the paper itself says 'limits independent replication of the specific execution payloads'? FALSIFIER: no source publishes a binding error rate in the four-part form, in which case the external-bar question is permanently unanswerable from literature, C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE is unoccupied-AND-unmeasured rather than settled, and the bar to beat must be set internally by Graph/Product. A negative here is only worth having if the search can actually fail, so the packet must also repair the design defects this audit exposed: (i) resolve every target name to a verified artifact identity BEFORE scoring any condition, and record 'not located' as unmeasured and never as a system-level negative - this is precisely how the mandated target COVENANT, 1 of 5, was silently substituted by arXiv:2608.02680 and lost; (ii) include a null control with power against the failure that actually occurred, e.g. substitute a deliberately wrong artifact identity and require the pipeline to flag it, since NC-FABRICATED-BINDING-CLAIMS searched for three literal phrases no paper would contain and detected nothing; (iii) require every reported number to carry its accounting convention and denominator, because the packet's strongest-looking figures were convention-dependent (6.4x is a TOTAL-STREAM-SPEND ratio while 25.65x is the per-item ratio for the same source, and that source also asserts an inconsistent 'three orders of magnitude'; 40x TCO hides an identical fixed 500 USD/month infrastructure line in every row; 18.2 microseconds is a trivial-artifact Node dispatch floor against the same paper's measured 65.7 ms compiled answer); and (iv) split addressing_open_nl_systems into 'open NL as compile input' and 'publishes a binding error rate', which here are 1 and 0, and treat MV2 as unsatisfiable-without-a-repository instead of passing it on paper claims.
